items.name: Max slope
items.source: NASA states a 20 deg capability for EVA walking [1]; the ARES planning limit is 15 deg (conservative margin).

items.name: Caution slope
items.source: ARES threshold. NASA notes that slopes above 10 deg are common at the lunar south pole and complicate traverses [2].

items.name: Walking speed
items.source: Based on Apollo-observed average walking speeds of 1.0 to 2.0 ft/s, about 1.1 to 2.2 km/h [3].

items.name: Note
items.source: No official human-on-Mars slope standard was found; the NASA values above are lunar and Artemis values. The Gale crater rover team routed Curiosity around a 23 deg slope via terrain under 15 deg [4].

items.name: Radiation dose rate
items.source: Published mean, not live: 0.64 ± 0.12 mSv/day dose equivalent, galactic cosmic rays only, Curiosity RAD at Gale, August 2012 to June 2013 near solar maximum [5]. Excludes solar particle events; 2026 values are likely higher.

items.name: EVA time limit
items.source: TO VERIFY: document supporting the 8 h limit on one EVA. The MARSWALK project notes list 8 h (reference architecture, Rucker & Hoffman 2020, HEOMD-415) but it was not checked against those documents.
